The YAML spec as sheets

Source: R/spec_sheets.R
tfl_sheets_from_yaml.Rd

tfl_sheets_from_yaml() reads a study's YAML spec and gives the sheets the workbooks held: for the app's grids and for the generators that still read sheets. The study's defaults are the rows with a blank output_id, a pattern's the @<name> rows, a report's its own rows (the files as written, not layered – the sheets' readers layer them as they always did). tfl_sheets_from_spec() does the same from a spec already read (or changed in memory, not written yet): tfl_sheets_from_yaml(dir) is tfl_sheets_from_spec(tfl_read_study_spec(dir), tfl_read_outputs(dir)).

Usage

tfl_sheets_from_yaml(dir)

tfl_sheets_from_spec(study, outputs)

Arguments

dir

The study folder (or its spec/).

study

The study's spec, as tfl_read_study_spec() reads it.

outputs

The reports, as tfl_read_outputs() reads them: a list of tfl_output (as written, not resolved), named by id.

Value

A list: table (the table and report sheets, with study), planner (the _tflplanner sheet: the report list and the setup), ard (the ARD sheets), listing (listings, listing_cols), figures (a figure's design list, by id), study (study.yml's fields), not_converted (what the sheets cannot hold).

Examples

d <- system.file("extdata", "spec-yaml", package = "tflspec")
sh <- tfl_sheets_from_yaml(d)
sh$planner$output_id
#> [1] NA         "T-14-1-1"
# the same from the spec in memory, a title changed and not written
s <- tfl_read_study_spec(d)
outs <- tfl_read_outputs(d)
outs[["T-14-1-1"]]$label <- "Demographics (draft)"
tfl_sheets_from_spec(s, outs)$planner$description
#> [1] "(every report)"       "Demographics (draft)"
